So we're looking to find the equation of the normal at the point $(8,5).$ For this, we need to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ which means we first need to find the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y\prime(t)}{x\prime(t)}=\frac{2 t}{4}.

$$
m=\frac{2(1)}{4}=\frac{1}{2}.

$$

$$
x=7{t}^{2}-9t+5,\,y={t}^{6}+2{t}^{2}+3,\,-\infty <t<\infty .
$$

Let $C$ be the point that corresponds to $t=1$ on the curve. Determine the coordinates of the point at which the normal to the curve at $C$ crosses the $y$-axis. Give exact answers.

The normal to the curve at $C$ crosses the $y$-axis at $(${{field-1}},
{{field-2}}$).$" :question/worked-solution "First, we find the coordinates of the point $C$ by substituting $t=1$ into the parametric equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =7({1}^{2})-9(1)+5=-2+5 \\ y & ={1}^{6}+2({1}^{2})+3=3+3\end{aligned}
$$

So, we're looking to determine the equation of the normal at the point $(3,6).$ For this, we need to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ which means we first need to find the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ as follows:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=14t-9,\,{y}^{′}(t)=6{t}^{5}+4t
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)} \\  & =\frac{6{t}^{5}+4t}{14t-9}.\end{aligned}
$$

At the point where $t=1,$ the slope of the tangent line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}m={\frac{dy}{dx}|}_{t\,=\,1} & =\frac{6({1}^{5})+4(1)}{14(1)-9} \\  & =\frac{10}{5} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope ${m}_{n}$ of the normal line, we take the negative reciprocal of $m:$

$$
{m}_{n}=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{2}
$$

To calculate the equation of the normal, we use point-slope form with the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(3,6)$ and the slope ${m}_{n}=-\frac{1}{2}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-3)-3 & =-\frac{1}{2}((x-5)-(-2)) \\ (y-3)-3 & =-\frac{1}{2}((x-5)+2) \\ (y-3)-3 & =-\frac{1}{2}(x-5)-1 \\ (y-3) & =-\frac{1}{2}(x-5)-1+3 \\ (y-3) & =-\frac{1}{2}(x-5)+2.\end{aligned}
$$

The normal crosses the $y$-axis when $x=0.$ At this point, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =- \frac{1}{2}(0-(3))+6 \\ y & =\frac{15}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
